# EU Digital Omnibus (2026 proposal)

## Summary

The Digital Omnibus is a European Commission proposal (COM(2025) 837 final, 19 November 2025) for a regulation on the simplification of the digital legislative framework. It amends the GDPR, the Data Act, the EUDPR and the ePrivacy Directive, and repeals the Free Flow of Data Regulation, the P2B Regulation, the Data Governance Act and the Open Data Directive, with staged application six to eighteen months after entry into force.

Documented GDPR amendments include: a narrowed, entity-relative personal-data definition (Article 4(1)); purpose-limitation and special-category adjustments; abusive-request handling (Article 12(5)); automated decision-making amendments (Article 22); breach notification via a single-entry point (Article 33); DPIA harmonization through EDPB lists and templates (Article 35); new Articles 88a (terminal-equipment consent), 88b (machine-readable choice signals) and 88c (a legitimate-interest basis for AI development and operation, subject to safeguards). The Data Act absorbs DGA Chapter II with new Articles 32a-32y.

## Applicability

This note applies as a watch item for the Brain's privacy and AI Act positions: it is a proposal, not adopted law. It explicitly does not amend the AI Act in this text — a separate companion proposal amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 is referenced but is not in the local corpus.

## Governance Considerations

- Do not assert Digital Omnibus changes as current obligations; track the legislative process before updating control requirements.
- If adopted as proposed: AI development and operation could rely on a safeguarded legitimate-interest basis (88c) — re-evaluate [legitimate-interest](/concepts/legitimate-interest.md) positions at that point; DPIA practice would move toward EDPB-issued lists and templates.
- Data governance programs absorbing DGA functions should track the Data Act absorption provisions.

## Limits

Proposal-stage instrument: all amendments cited are draft law. The companion AI Act amending proposal is absent from the corpus — no claim is made here about AI Act timeline or substantive changes. Correlation-table annexes (SRC-0013) contain no substantive rules.

## Related Concepts

- [gdpr](/concepts/gdpr.md) is the principal statute amended.
- [legitimate-interest](/concepts/legitimate-interest.md) is the basis the draft Article 88c would extend to AI development.
- [eu-ai-act](/concepts/eu-ai-act.md) is amended by the separate companion proposal (not in corpus).
- [edpb](/concepts/edpb.md) receives proposal-stage new roles (DPIA lists and templates).
